text:
alex: Quick draft of a reproducible quant benchmark methodology for FP8/INT8/4-bit runs — want focused review on warmup procedure, power cap handling, tokenization parity, and KV cache effects.

maya: Dropping an initial proposal + a runnable command. Trying to keep things deterministic and fair across backends.

maya: Run command we used for yesterday's notebook (example):
```
# example benchmark driver (bash)
./run_quant_bench \
  --model-path /mnt/models/llama-70b/quant/llama-70b-int8q \
  --seq-len 2048 \
  --batch-shape "[1,2,4]" \
  --warmup-steps 250 \
  --measure-steps 1000 \
  --powercap-watts 250 \
  --kv-policy shared_prefix_cache \
  --tokenizer-normalize true \
  --deterministic-seed 42 \
  --profile kernels,kv,batching,power \
  --out results/run-${THREAD_TS}.json
```

liam: Why 250 warmup? feels high for int8 microbenchmarks. Can we do an adaptive warmup instead?

maya: 250 was chosen to ensure steady-state for KV-heavy workloads (lots of prefix reuse). But agreed we should test adaptive warmup. Proposed adaptive heuristic: run until 3 consecutive measurements of per-step latency are within 2% of running median, up to a cap of 500 steps.

sophia: Important: warmup must include realistic tokenization/prefix patterns. Don't just feed repeated tokens — use a 50/50 split of fresh vs cached prefixes to exercise KV cache eviction and refill.

alex: Also: enforce identical tokenization across quantized and fp16 comparisons (same tokenizer version, same whitespace normalization flags). Small tokenization diffs skew perf by changing branching and KV hits.

devex: Logging checklist for each run (so dashboards can automatically compare):
- model + quant scheme (FP16/FP8/INT8/4bit)
- kernel version + kernel selection flags
- powercap (watts) and measured package power time series
- warmup heuristic used (fixed/adaptive + steps)
- batch shapes and request arrival pattern (poisson/constant)

infra-bot: deploy: perf-agent v2.3 started on node pool "dedicated-bench" for run 1833724800-01 :rocket:

liam: For fair comparisons: lock sequence length distribution and batch shape sampling seed. If we compare fp16 vs int8, ensure identical request scheduling and pinned CPU affinities to avoid jitter from noisy neighbors.

maya: Calibration note: when doing per-channel calibration (min/max or KL), record calibration dataset used and quant stats. Calibration can change cache footprints (activations bit patterns) which affect kernel paths.

sophia: Also record fallback count: how many times runtime fell back from quant kernel to float kernel due to out-of-range values or numerical safety checks. That can explain perf regressions.

alex: Perf regressions triage flow proposal:
1) reproduce locally with same seed + same powercap + same warmup heuristic.
2) capture kernel-level flamegraph and NVTX ranges around KV get/put and attention kernels.
3) compare calibration histograms and activation ranges.
4) if fallback triggers, log exact tensor and op where fallback happened.

devex: Example JSON output we want per-run (compact):
```
{
  "run_id": "1833724800-01",
  "model": "llama-70b-int8q",
  "quant": "int8-asym-phase0",
  "kernel_commit": "a3f9b2",
  "powercap": "250W",
  "warmup": "adaptive(250->320)",
  "kv_policy": "shared_prefix_cache",
  "metrics": {
    "p50_ms": "123.4",
    "p95_ms": "210.1",
    "tokens_per_sec": "45.6"
  },
  "fallbacks": 2
}
```

liam: One more: include a small tokenization sample (first 64 tokens / initial prompt) so quality regression teams can repro outputs if needed.

maya: On powercap: we saw non-linear perf cliffs when hitting thermal limits on older nodes. Recommendation: run the same workload across 3 power settings (nominal, -10%, -20%) and report normalized throughput per watt.

alex: Good. Also add kernel selection matrix to results: for each op type (attention, matmul, gelu) list which kernel was chosen and why (latency heuristic or fallback).

sophia: For KV cache behavior: capture KV hit rate over time and average KV memory working set. If we see oscillation, include per-iteration KV eviction count.

devex: Can someone add a short ci-job that runs the methodology on a small fixture model daily? That would catch drifting regressions from runtime changes.

maya: I'll sketch a small CI job using a 1-step-per-batch scaled-down run and upload the template to the perf repo by EOD.

alex: Thanks — next steps: maya to PR config + ci job; liam and sophia to validate adaptive warmup heuristic on two workloads (kv-heavy, purely autoregressive); devex to add json schema for run output. We'll reconvene after first automated runs. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: run 1833724800-01 finished: p50=124.1ms, p95=212.8ms, tokens/s=44.9, fallbacks=2

maya: Uploaded results and a short writeup: https://go/bench-root/1833724800-01 (internal). Please comment if anything missing.

liam: Looks good. Small nit: please include GPU frequency governor state at start of run.

alex: Adding that to checklist. Thanks everyone.
